pages.text:
Super Micro sees quarterly revenue soaring on AI server boom
Hewlett Packard Enterprise, Miami HEAT to Improve Wireless Reliability at Kaseya Center
Miami Heat Selects Hewlett Packard Enterprise to Modernize Wireless and Wired Infrastructure At Kaseya Center, with At&T and Cspi Technology Solutions to Support the Networking Environment
Miami HEAT selected HPE to modernize both its wireless and wired infrastructure and establish Wi-Fi 7 connectivity. This connectivity refresh is part of a series of updates being made to the venue ahead of the 2026-2027 NBA season to improve the arena experience for attendees. The deployment combines HPE Aruba wireless outdoor and indoor access points and campus gateways with HPE Juniper switching that provides the power, bandwidth and capacity required to support high-density connectivity throughout the venue.
HPE will also provide Arena Event Network Monitoring Assistance across five live events to help validate and optimize network performance under real-world conditions. HPE?s AI-native networking capabilities are designed to help organizations move from reactive network management toward increasingly autonomous operations. HPE?s self-driving network uses AI-driven insights and automation to proactively identify and resolve connectivity issues, optimize performance and simplify troubleshooting, which helps IT teams maintain reliable connectivity while reducing the operational burden of managing increasingly complex environments.
For a high-density venue such as Kaseya Center, this approach provides the Miami HEAT with a scalable foundation to support evolving connectivity demands across basketball games, concerts and other major events. The wireless deployment is expected to be completed ahead of the start of the 2026-2027 NBA season, with the broader campus switching modernization continuing in phases across the venue. HPE is working with AT&T, which will provide communication services and CSPi Technology Solutions that will provide implementation expertise and ongoing managed IT services to support the networking environment.

pages.title: Hewlett Packard Enterprise Just Surged 40% in a Month: Take Profits, or Buy More? - AOL
pages.text:
HPE surged 40% in one month, driven by a $1.2 billion Vultr AI rack order and a raised networking revenue growth outlook near 20%.
SMCI and DELL gained only 13% and 11% over the same period, confirming HPE's move as a company-specific re-rating, not a broad sector rally.
The 40% one-month run prices in years of unproven targets, with a single customer order and $800 million in Juniper savings as the only support.
Just released. Our analysts combed the entire stock market and named the ten best stocks to buy right now, and Hewlett Packard Enterprise didn't make the cut. Enter your email to see the names that beat HPE. The report is free. Enter your email and see if any of your stocks made the cut.
Hewlett Packard Enterprise (NYSE:HPE) has spent the past month convincing the market that its networking business drives its role in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure. Shares of Hewlett Packard Enterprise are trading at $72.70, up 40% over the past month, after two company announcements reset expectations for that business.
HPE Price Target — 24/7 Wall St.
Meanwhile, Super Micro Computer (NASDAQ:SMCI) stock is at $44.79, up 13% over the same period, a solid gain that still trails Hewlett Packard Enterprise stock by a wide margin. For its part, Dell Technologies (NYSE:DELL) stock is at $580.40, up 11% over the past month, a pace similar to that of Super Micro Computer stock.
For sector-wide gauges, the iShares U.S. Technology ETF (NYSEARCA:IYW) is at $271.51 and the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) trades at $757.24; these funds are up 7% and 5%, respectively, over the past month. That spread, with Hewlett Packard Enterprise stock far ahead of both rivals and both funds, marks a company-specific re-rating inside a sector that rose at a much slower clip.
Why Didn't HPE Make The Top 10 List?
24/7 Wall St has helped investors make money for over two decades, and our top analysts just finished ranking the definitive Top 10 Stocks To Buy Now. Not the ten biggest companies. Not the ten everyone is arguing about. The ten best stocks to buy right now.
And HPE didn't make the cut!
The report is free, and you can see why we think each stock is a top investment today.
A Helios Order and a Higher Networking Outlook
On September 30, Hewlett Packard Enterprise secured its first order for Helios AI rack systems, a $1.2 billion agreement with cloud provider Vultr covering deployments across Vultr's data centers in the United States. Under that deal, Hewlett Packard Enterprise is providing the networking layer, including Ethernet switches built on its Juniper technology, along with liquid cooling and deployment services.
At an investor day the same day, Hewlett Packard Enterprise raised its networking revenue growth outlook for the coming fiscal year into a high-teens to low-twenties percentage range. The company also set long-term targets. It projected its data center networking revenue to compound at a low-to-high fifties percentage rate over the following years, and it targeted its networking operating margins in the mid-to-high twenties as a percentage.
Why Networking Sets Hewlett Packard Enterprise Apart
Hewlett Packard Enterprise sells servers, storage and networking to data center operators, and the Juniper acquisition made networking the part of its business carrying the growth story. Because of that shift, a networking outlook carries outsized weight for Hewlett Packard Enterprise stock. Even the Vultr relationship traces back to Juniper, since Hewlett Packard Enterprise inherited it through that acquisition.
Super Micro Computer assembles servers built around other companies' processors, with little services revenue beside them. Dell sells servers and storage into the same buyers, with a large services business attached. All three capture data center spending, yet only Hewlett Packard Enterprise is being valued on a networking franchise.
Both September 30 announcements from Hewlett Packard Enterprise fell inside the past-month window, and they separate the company from Super Micro Computer and Dell. Shares of each of those rivals climbed over the same month while trailing Hewlett Packard Enterprise stock by a wide margin, and the two technology funds advanced by less still.
HPE Analyst Ratings — 24/7 Wall St.
The Vultr order supports the case for Hewlett Packard Enterprise, showing the company can win the networking layer of an AI buildout on top of the servers. Hewlett Packard Enterprise's raised savings target adds support, since the company now expects $800 million in annual run-rate cost savings from the Juniper acquisition, a figure that makes the deal look stronger than before.
A 40% gain in Hewlett Packard Enterprise stock in a single month, however, prices a great deal of that progress into the share price. Several pieces of the company's outlook cover years that haven't happened yet, and one order from one customer still amounts to a single data point.
Super Micro Computer stock and Dell stock rising far less over the same month is what makes the move in Hewlett Packard Enterprise stock company-specific, a distinction that cuts both ways since a re-rating built on one company's announcements could reverse if Hewlett Packard Enterprise's next update falls short.
Investors can watch for a second Helios platform customer, which would show whether the Vultr order at Hewlett Packard Enterprise begins a pattern, as a follow-on win would strengthen the case for the company's networking push while a long gap could leave Hewlett Packard Enterprise stock leaning on one deal.
Shareholders may want to keep an eye on whether Hewlett Packard Enterprise's networking growth rate holds within the high-teens to low-twenties percentage range the company outlined for the coming fiscal year. Reaching that range would support Hewlett Packard Enterprise stock at its new level, while a slowdown could hand back part of the past month's gain.
Hewlett Packard Enterprise now pairs a stronger networking story with a far higher share price than a month ago. Share positions should reflect both the promise of the Vultr order and the speed of a 40% one-month run in HPE stock.

pages.text:

HPE Spaceborne Computer to Power High Performance Computing and AI on the Moon
HPE Spaceborne Computer-4, an advanced compute module built for space environments, plans to power artificial intelligence (AI) and the first high performance computing (HPC) benchmarks on the surface of the Moon.
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 9:00 AM CDT 5 min read
NASA, Deloitte, and HPE to deploy AI workloads on HPE's Spaceborne Computer-4 to maximize the mission's scientific discovery
With 70 years of leadership in space exploration, HPE ushers in a new era by providing the advanced computing foundation for the emerging lunar economy
HPE Spaceborne Computer-4 plans to power the first high performance computing benchmarks on the lunar surface
HPE Spaceborne Computer-4 will test large language model (LLM) retrieval-augmented generation, vision inference, and LiDAR data for reliable deployment of AI on the Moon
HOUSTON, October 20, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--HPE today announced HPE Spaceborne Computer-4, an advanced compute module built for space environments, plans to power artificial intelligence (AI) and the first high performance computing (HPC) benchmarks on the surface of the Moon1. The system will deploy on Astrolab's FLIP rover for an upcoming mission for the Moon Base program and will test the suitability of advanced computing for future missions and the emerging lunar economy.
"For more than 70 years, HPE innovation has supported some of the world's most important space missions. The next chapter of lunar exploration will depend on the ability to turn data into insights at the point of discovery," said Scott Wiest, vice president, fellow and global sales chief technologist, HPE. "With HPE Spaceborne Computer-4, we are bringing AI and high performance computing to the lunar edge, helping the acceleration of scientific discovery and building the infrastructure for the next era of exploration."
The mission is intended to launch in late 2026 as part of NASA's Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) initiative. After touching down near the lunar South Pole region, Voyager Technologies' Griffin-1 lander will transport Astrolab's FLIP rover, carrying HPE Spaceborne Computer-4 as a payload.
"The Moon presents a challenging environment for advanced computing, and we're pleased to provide HPE with an opportunity to demonstrate its technology on the lunar surface," said Jaret Matthews, founder and CEO of Astrolab. "Our FLIP rover is designed to accommodate a variety of payloads, and this mission will demonstrate how commercial lunar mobility platforms can support technology development and scientific research."
AI workloads and first-ever HPC to run on the Moon's surface
During the mission, HPE Spaceborne Computer-4 is scheduled to run core AI applications and the first high performance computing2 benchmarks on the Moon. The test results from these experiments will help create the technological foundation required for future missions and research on the Moon's surface. Large language models (LLM) will deliver insights, analyze visual data, and support autonomous monitoring at the lunar edge. Additional tests will process LiDAR data for mapping, navigation, terrain analysis and infrastructure development, while an AI services container will demonstrate reliable deployment of scalable AI service applications on the Moon.
HPE Spaceborne Computer-4 is purpose-built as a lightweight, self-contained, and fanless compute module designed to survive the harsh environment of the lunar South pole. It is equipped with both a low-power central process unit (CPU) and graphics processing unit (GPU). The compute module utilizes flash memory storage inside solid state drives from KIOXIA, continuing a long-standing collaboration with the HPE Spaceborne program to support the missions' activities and tests with high performance data storage under lunar conditions. HPE also assembled an extensive software suite that optimizes the required interaction with Earth-based resources and enables secure delivery of insights and results from the Moon back to Earth.
In addition, HPE will support Astrolab's mission control in Hawthorne, California using HPE Private Cloud to support real-time insights, delivered in a turnkey solution. In addition, HPE CloudOps Software will provide a unified, flexible environment for managing and automating workloads.
Private-public partnerships help maximize the mission's scientific return
NASA and Deloitte are set to join HPE Spaceborne Computer-4 to deploy AI workloads on the Moon and perform advanced solutions critical for maximizing the scientific return, underpinning the success of the emerging lunar economy.
Utilizing the Federated Learning for Unbounded and Intelligent Decentralization (FLUID) experiment, NASA will run an AI neural net model trained on data from Earth, the Moon, and on the International Space Station, demonstrating coordination of three separate AI models. NASA will also conduct a tuned LLM test with semantic processing abilities to assist in searching and interpreting onboard documents.
Deloitte's Silent Shield™, a new system to detect cyber intrusions, will provide near real-time, predictive cyber-analytics and anomaly detection.
Building on the years of successful deployment on the International Space Station, HPE Spaceborne Computer-4 is the latest successor to the HPE Spaceborne Computer project that will deliver real-time, advanced data processing to the newest frontiers of far-edge computing.
HPE (NYSE: HPE) is a leader in essential enterprise technology, bringing together the power of AI, cloud, and networking to help organizations achieve more. As pioneers of possibility, our innovation and expertise advance the way people live and work. We empower our customers across industries to optimize operational performance, transform data into foresight, and maximize their impact. Unlock your boldest ambitions with HPE. Discover more at www.hpe.com.
1 Based on analysis of publicly available information as of October 20, 2026, no other company or organization has conducted the specific HPC benchmarks that HPE plans to execute on the surface of the Moon, nor will any planned mission with HPC by other parties take place on the Moon prior to HPE's mission.
2 HPE Spaceborne Computer-4 to run high-performance LINPACK (HPL) and high-performance conjugate gradient (HPCG) on the surface of the Moon.
As used in this document, "Deloitte" means Deloitte Consulting LLP, a subsidiary of Deloitte LLP. Please see www.deloitte.com/us/about for a detailed description of our legal structure. Certain services may not be available to attest clients under the rules and regulations of public accounting.

HPE Has a 12x Forward PE and 400% Growth. So Why Won’t Wall Street Touch It?
HPE just posted its worst week ever after a single analyst downgrade, yet its earnings are surging and its backlog hit a record high. The real question is whether the market sees a danger that the numbers are hiding.
Published October 20, 2026, 7:31am ET · 4 min read
Two professionals analyze market data and financial trends on a laptop, mirroring the optimistic outlook and raised price targets for companies like HPE. © VideoFlow / Shutterstock.com
Shares of Hewlett Packard Enterprise (NYSE:HPE | HPE Price Prediction) fell 20.56% in the week through October 19. It was its worst week ever, following an October 14 analyst downgrade that questioned HPE’s AI growth.
The drop hit a stock that already traded at a forward PE of roughly 12 to 15, while the broader market averages 30. Investors Dave Ahern and Stephen Morris recently debated whether that gap makes HPE an opportunity or a value trap.
Ahern asked: “Is that a lifetime opportunity, or does Wall Street know something that the rest of value investors maybe don’t know? Like, why is it so cheap?” The question is pressing because the results are strong.
Revenue in the fiscal third quarter rose 32.7% to $12.21 billion. Non-GAAP EPS of $1.11 beat the $0.93 consensus.
Morris rated HPE’s moat today as “next to non-existent,” and that view accounts for most of the discount.
A 12x Multiple Signals Doubt About Durability
A forward PE divides the share price by expected earnings. A low multiple therefore means investors doubt those estimates will hold, and the market is currently pricing in a fade in AI server demand.
The trailing P/E of 1300x is distorted by Juniper integration charges and a fiscal 2025 goodwill impairment. That is why the hosts focus on the forward number.
Analysts’ average fiscal 2027 EPS estimate is $4.7088, up from $4.0384 90 days ago. None of those analysts revised down in the past 30 days.
Management’s own fiscal 2027 framework calls for EPS of $4.40 to $4.60. That range leaves out the Helios AI rack opportunity.
Wall Street Turned Cautious After a Huge Run
Even after falling 8.05% over the past month, HPE is still up 135.22% year to date and 147.52% over the past year. Shares rose 1.29% on October 19 to $55.84. The post-downgrade rebound was small.
Although the market has embraced HPE this year, it remains unclear whether AI-driven earnings will last long enough to justify that price. Still, orders grew faster than revenue, and backlog hit a record while memory shortages held back shipments.
Ahern’s long-term test sets the hype aside: “Forget the AI trade. What is a stock going to do 10 years from now?” AI server revenue fails that test because it is cyclical: orders shrink once data center buildouts slow, and nothing ties buyers to HPE.
Server revenue rose 35.3% to $6.77 billion on AI demand. Servers are a competitive, low-margin business, and customers switch suppliers over price, which is why the picks-and-shovels names behind the AI expansion (power, cooling, networking) often look more durable than the box makers; we rounded up seven of them in a free report here.
Management expects gross margin to return to historical levels as AI systems take up a larger share of sales. It guides Cloud and AI operating margin to about 13% in fiscal 2027.
Juniper Is HPE’s First Real Shot at a Moat
HPE closed its Juniper Networks acquisition and sold its remaining 19% stake in China-based H3C in May 2026. Together, those moves changed its business mix toward networking.
Networking gear is built into how a customer runs its operations, and it costs a lot to replace. The segment earned a 22% operating margin last quarter. With Juniper included, networking revenue jumped 74.9% to $2.89 billion, and orders rose 36%.
GreenLake lets customers pay for infrastructure as a service inside their own data centers, and it reached 52,000 customers, up 18%. Rising net retention would point to recurring revenue, while flat usage would suggest customers use it to finance hardware.
Discussing the chief executive’s vision, Morris said “the uncertainty around that statement is very high,” but added that if it “comes to fruition,” HPE “will be significantly untouchable.” Juniper likely moves HPE’s moat from absent to plausible, although the integration still has to prove it can hold customers.
HPE’s case looks strongest under Ahern’s 10-year test. The weekly drop and a forward multiple far below the market’s already price in heavy doubt.
Juniper savings are on track for a $600 million annual run rate by fiscal 2028. Meanwhile, a 1.07% dividend yield on a $74.1 billion company provides some income.
The thesis breaks if networking growth stalls after the integration, if GreenLake fails to become recurring revenue, or if AI server demand falls faster than networking can make up for it. Fiscal fourth-quarter results come next. Revenue is guided to $13.9 billion to $14.8 billion, and management has promised a fuller fiscal 2027 outlook.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) Stock: Rises as Miami HEAT Taps HPE for Wi-Fi 7 Upgrade
HPE Stock Gains as Miami HEAT Selects Wi-Fi 7 Technology to Modernize Kaseya Center Ahead of NBA Season
By Yasmin WernerOctober 19, 2026No Comments3 Mins Read
HPE stock climbs 1.29% to $55.84 following a new Miami HEAT networking deal.
Miami HEAT taps HPE to bring faster Wi-Fi 7 connectivity to Kaseya Center fans.
HPE Aruba access points and Juniper switches will modernize arena connectivity.
HPE will test and optimize arena network performance across five live events.
AT&T and CSPi will support the network rollout ahead of the 2026–27 NBA season.
Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) stock gained 1.29% to close at $55.84 on Monday, October 19. Shares added 0.05% to $55.87 after hours, despite afternoon selling pressure. HPE also announced a Miami HEAT project to upgrade Kaseya Center’s connectivity.
HPE Stock Advances as Arena Upgrades Expand
HPE will overhaul wireless access and supporting wired systems ahead of the 2026–27 NBA season. For the Miami HEAT, the project forms part of broader improvements to the venue’s digital infrastructure. These improvements target fan access, staff communication, and systems that support daily arena operations.
Kaseya Center hosts basketball games, concerts, and other events that attract large crowds. Heavy device use can strain wireless networks, especially where spectators sit close together. The HEAT initially focused on improving coverage in crowded seating sections, including the lower bowl.
However, a technical review showed that faster wireless access also required upgrades to existing wired equipment. As a result, the project expanded to address network switching and power delivery. The broader scope will help the venue handle modern access points and future digital services.
Wi-Fi 7 Upgrade Targets High-Density Connectivity
Under the plan, HPE will install Aruba indoor and outdoor wireless access points across the site. Campus gateways will manage traffic, while HPE Juniper switches will supply the required bandwidth and capacity. Together, the equipment will establish Wi-Fi 7 connectivity for fans and staff.
Wi-Fi 7 supports greater network capacity in busy locations with large numbers of connected devices. At Kaseya Center, the upgrade targets reliable performance during games and other major events. It also aims to limit connection problems in critical seating areas and operational spaces.
HPE will provide specialized network monitoring support during five live events. Those sessions will test network behavior under real crowds and changing traffic conditions. Engineers can then tune performance using event data rather than relying only on initial tests.
HPE plans to use AI-assisted network tools to identify faults and improve performance. Its automation can simplify troubleshooting and reduce manual work for arena technology teams. This approach will support network operations as demand changes across different event schedules.
AT&T will provide communication services for the updated network environment. CSPi Technology Solutions will supply implementation support and ongoing managed IT services. These roles will connect the hardware deployment with its practical operation after installation.
HPE expects to finish the wireless rollout before the new NBA season starts. The company will continue switching upgrades across the arena in phases. For HPE, the agreement extends its networking work into another high-traffic entertainment setting.

Learn Why The Bull Case For HPE Stock Could Change Following Gen13 Server Launch
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 7:22 PM CDT 6 min read
Hewlett Packard Enterprise announced its first HPE ProLiant Gen13 Servers powered by 6th Gen AMD EPYC processors, adding higher core density, expanded memory and I/O, and new security features such as automatic self encrypting drives, multi person authorization, and extended post quantum cryptography readiness.
The ProLiant Gen13 lineup targets AI inference, agentic AI workflows, data intensive simulations, and financial modeling, which speaks directly to HPE's push into higher value compute, security centric infrastructure, and rack level efficiency for customers modernizing data centers and hybrid cloud environments.
We will now look at how Hewlett Packard Enterprise's investment narrative could be influenced by these ProLiant Gen13 AI focused servers.
Activate your watchlist for AI infrastructure by scanning our handpicked 55 AI infrastructure stocks, which are building the compute and cooling backbone for workloads similar to Hewlett Packard Enterprise's latest announcements.
Hewlett Packard Enterprise Investment Narrative Recap
An investor in Hewlett Packard Enterprise needs to believe the business can turn strong AI and networking demand into delivered systems, higher margin services, and durable recurring revenue. The latest ProLiant Gen13 and Cray XD launches point to that direction, but the near term swing factor still looks like execution on AI infrastructure orders and Juniper integration rather than any single product win.
The biggest near term risk remains a mismatch between robust orders and what actually ships into data center and hybrid cloud projects, especially now that guidance already incorporates healthy AI server and networking expectations. Valuation stretch and insider selling add sensitivity to any slip in AI deal timing, networking CAGRs, or margin delivery.
The Mizuho Securities deployment of HPE Cray XD2000 with direct liquid cooling is the clearest operational tie in to the new ProLiant Gen13 story. Both point to Hewlett Packard Enterprise leaning into high density, liquid cooled compute for workloads that resemble AI training and inference, complex financial modeling, and large scale simulations.
For catalysts, this type of reference project matters because it tests HPE's ability to scale advanced cooling, maintain performance per kilowatt, and wrap it with monitoring and services. Any delays in bringing the new Mizuho data center into production or in expanding beyond the initial eight nodes would feed directly into the existing risk around converting AI infrastructure demand into recognized revenue.
Hewlett Packard Enterprise Forecasts Behind the AI Server Push
Hewlett Packard Enterprise's AI centric server roadmap plugs into a much bigger earnings story that analysts have already mapped out. The projections assume the business can convert ProLiant Gen13, Cray XD, and Juniper powered networking into steadier profit instead of just one off hardware spikes.
Consensus forecasts point to Hewlett Packard Enterprise's revenue rising by 14.3% a year over the next three years, with earnings expected to climb from US$2.7b today to US$6.1b by 2029. That implies earnings a little more than doubling from the current base if the forecast plays out as modeled.
On top of that profit bridge, analysts are baking in margin expansion from 6.4% today to 9.8% in three years, helped by a higher mix from AI infrastructure, data center networking, and recurring GreenLake style services tied to deployments like the new ProLiant Gen13 servers. The story is not just about selling more hardware. It is about attaching software, monitoring, and financing so that more of each data center dollar shows up as net income.
Those expectations are not perfectly aligned. Some research teams see earnings reaching as high as US$7.3b by 2029, which would require an even stronger uplift from AI centric networking and data center projects than the base case. For readers, that spread in outcomes is a reminder to stress test personal models for slower AI uptake, longer Juniper integration timelines, or more muted margin progress alongside the upside scenarios.
Valuation assumptions sit on top of these operating forecasts. To support current analyst targets, Hewlett Packard Enterprise would need to trade on a P/E of 19.9x applied to the 2029 earnings estimate, compared with 34.1x today. That would represent a lower multiple than the 27.4x currently cited for the broader US tech industry, which places more of the burden on actual execution in AI infrastructure rather than on multiple expansion.
Hewlett Packard Enterprise's narrative projects US$62.5b revenue and US$6.1b earnings by 2029. This requires 14.3% yearly revenue growth and an earnings increase from US$2.7b.

One alternate angle focuses on Juniper integration risk rather than ProLiant or Cray demand. The most cautious Hewlett Packard Enterprise analysts were working off revenue of US$58.9b and earnings of US$5.6b by 2029, paired with a 15.9x P/E. Those estimates came before this news, so you may see views shift once analysts revisit their models.

Editor: David Moadel.

Servers are the lifeblood of software systems.

© Tommy Lee Walker AI server makers are bouncing back together after a sharp hardware selloff last week. Super Micro Computer (NASDAQ:SMCI | SMCI Price Prediction) stock is up 4% to $32.87 in morning trading, leading the group. Meanwhile, Hewlett Packard Enterprise (NYSE:HPE) stock is up 3% to $57.01, just behind Super Micro Computer stock. Dell Technologies (NYSE:DELL) stock is up 2% to $462.64, though Hewlett Packard Enterprise stock rose more. For a broader read on tech, the iShares U.S. Technology ETF (NYSEARCA:IYW) is up 1.59%. Alongside it, the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) is up 1.55%, putting AI hardware at the front of a broader tech rebound. Last week’s slide in Dell and Hewlett Packard Enterprise stock followed a Barclays report that downgraded both companies to Equal Weight on valuation. The Barclays report highlighted possible server and storage pressure as memory prices normalize. Shares of Dell led a broad data center selloff last Wednesday, with Super Micro Computer stock slipping alongside it. Hewlett Packard Enterprise stock went on to log its worst week ever. Super Micro Computer named Mark Long, who previously led finance at a major storage maker, as its chief financial officer last week, replacing David Weigand. The appointment lands as Super Micro Computer scales a business that builds rack-scale AI servers on thin margins. In its Q4 FY2026 report, Super Micro Computer posted revenue of $11.12 billion, up 93.2% year over year, slightly missing the $11.56 billion estimate. Founder Charles Liang spoke on the earnings call. He described the shortfall as “purely a timing story,” citing short-term customer delays tied to power, cooling and networking. A better enterprise customer mix lifted Super Micro Computer’s GAAP gross margin to 17.5% from 9.5% a year earlier. Even so, the company guided Q1 FY2027 gross margin to just 10.4% to 10.8%, a reminder of how thin its AI server economics can run. For Mark Long, cash generation is central to his new role at Super Micro Computer. During Q4, the company produced $722 million of free cash flow while its inventory rose to $12.9 billion ahead of expected FY2027 growth. With its $7.5 billion in cash and net debt down to $1.2 billion, the company enters Long’s tenure with more balance-sheet room than it had a quarter earlier. Super Micro Computer now faces a key question: can its new finance chief steady the company’s cash flow. Its FY2027 guidance calls for revenue of $65 billion to $72 billion after more than $60 billion in new orders during FY2026, and funding that growth could keep its working capital stretched. On the August earnings call, Liang asserted, “The demand for our AI IT solutions is even stronger than ever before.” Whether Super Micro Computer’s inventory begins converting into cash as its record backlog ships is worth tracking. Dell and Hewlett Packard Enterprise stock remain tied to last week’s Barclays debate over valuation and memory prices. A sharp bounce in Super Micro Computer, Dell and Hewlett Packard Enterprise stock could fade quickly if last week’s worries return. Over the past 5 years, Hewlett Packard Enterprise has returned 315.2%, which raises the stakes on whether that performance is fully backed by the cash the company can generate.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise Falls 5% as AI Financing Worries Extend Hardware Selloff; Super Micro Sinks 7%, Dell Drops 3%
AI hardware stocks are cracking under a debate investors cannot yet resolve: who actually pays for the data center buildout, and whether the revenue surge was ever what it seemed.
Published October 16, 2026, 11:42am ET · 3 min read
Market Movers desk. Editor: David Moadel.
Worries over how the AI infrastructure boom gets paid for are rippling through hardware stocks again. Hewlett Packard Enterprise (NYSE:HPE | HPE Price Prediction) stock is down 5% at $55.87 this morning, extending a selloff that has swept across the biggest names in AI servers.
Meanwhile, Super Micro Computer (NASDAQ:SMCI) stock is down 7% to $32.78, a larger slide than Hewlett Packard Enterprise stock. Dell Technologies (NYSE:DELL) stock is down 3% to $458.78, a softer decline than Hewlett Packard Enterprise stock.
Servers, storage and networking equipment make up the Hewlett Packard Enterprise lineup, while Dell sells servers, storage and PCs. Super Micro Computer builds AI-optimized servers, giving it a more direct tie to AI data center buildouts than Hewlett Packard Enterprise or Dell.
AI Financing Doubts Extend the Hardware Selloff
Pressure on Hewlett Packard Enterprise stock extends a selloff in AI hardware as investors question how AI infrastructure spending gets financed. Data center buildouts demand heavy upfront expenditures. Doubts about who funds them flow straight back to the companies that sell the equipment, including Hewlett Packard Enterprise. We pulled together seven suppliers riding that same expansion, from power to cooling and networking, in a free report here.
Barclays heightened that debate on Wednesday when it cut its ratings on Hewlett Packard Enterprise and Dell to the equivalent of hold. The firm argued that businesses haven’t yet meaningfully increased their AI spending and that recent hardware revenue strength owes more to higher memory component prices.
Broader technology funds are slipping by smaller margins. The iShares U.S. Technology ETF (NYSEARCA:IYW) is down 2%. Large-cap tech is holding up even better (though it’s still selling off), as the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) is down 1.3%.
Networking Growth Versus Component Price Risk
The upside story for Hewlett Packard Enterprise rests on AI server demand and its expanded networking business. Networking gives the company a second growth engine alongside servers, which could buffer Hewlett Packard Enterprise if AI server orders cool.
Hewlett Packard Enterprise is still integrating Juniper Networks into its networking business, so much of the payoff depends on execution. Integration work can absorb management focus at a time when hardware demand faces fresh questions.
On the bear side, slower enterprise AI spending could leave the hardware growth at Hewlett Packard Enterprise tied to component prices. Under that view, revenue could cool once memory pricing settles down, even if customer orders hold steady.
Corporate AI budgets sit at the center of this debate. Will businesses begin to lift that spending? The next test for Hewlett Packard Enterprise is whether they do so in a way that backs up its server and networking story. Clear signs of broader enterprise adoption could ease the financing worries weighing on Hewlett Packard Enterprise stock.
Memory pricing is the other open variable for Hewlett Packard Enterprise, since Barclays tied much of the recent hardware revenue strength to higher component prices. Investors can watch for whether the gap between Hewlett Packard Enterprise stock and the broader technology funds (IYW and QQQ) narrows as the financing debate plays out.
Hewlett Packard Enterprise still holds a credible growth path through AI servers and its expanded networking business, but the hardware group is trading on financing doubts for now. Traders may prefer to keep their HPE share exposure small until the enterprise AI spending question resolves.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise (NYSE:HPE) introduced its AI focused ProLiant Gen13 server lineup, targeting next generation workloads and security needs.
The firm announced new AI ready ProLiant systems positioned for higher computing efficiency in enterprise data centers.
Mizuho Securities selected HPE's direct liquid cooled Cray XD2000 infrastructure for large scale financial simulations and complex modeling.
The ProLiant Gen13 launch and Mizuho liquid cooled deal only capture one side of how HPE's AI infrastructure story is evolving. Take a look at 2 warning signs we have identified for Hewlett Packard Enterprise.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise develops infrastructure and data solutions across the US and international markets, so these AI centric servers and liquid cooled systems fit directly into its role supplying large institutions with hardware for intensive computing and analytics workloads.

HPE's AI hardware push leans into the networking-led Narrative, but leaves one execution gap wide open
Hewlett Packard Enterprise's Narrative hinges on using AI-centric networking, data-center infrastructure and cloud services to tilt the mix toward recurring, higher margin revenue, and these Gen13 servers and liquid-cooled wins plug directly into that story.
"The main factor that has to go right is successful execution on the Juniper integration and the AI networking build out, so that the company captures the growth and cost synergies implied by the higher networking CAGRs, margin targets and long term supply commitments…"

The unresolved issue is still conversion of AI-heavy orders into recognized networking revenue at the pace implied by those high CAGRs. Long deployment timelines, liquid-cooling buildouts and the need to integrate Juniper gear cleanly all sit on the same choke point that analysts have flagged as a key risk for this story.

pages.title: Dell Falls 8% as Barclays Cuts Rating and Target to $574; Hewlett Packard Enterprise Drops 5%, Super Micro Computer Slides 4% - 24/7 Wall St.
pages.text:
Dell Falls 8% as Barclays Cuts Rating and Target to $574; Hewlett Packard Enterprise Drops 5%, Super Micro Computer Slides 4% Barclays just pulled the rug on two of the biggest names in AI server hardware, and the selloff raises a question every enterprise tech investor needs to answer: how much AI growth is already baked into these stocks? Published October 14, 2026, 11:34am ET · 3 min read Market Movers desk. Editor: David Moadel.

Servers are the lifeblood of software systems.

© Tommy Lee Walker Dell Technologies (NYSE:DELL | DELL Price Prediction) stock is down 8% to $526.86 in morning trading after Barclays cut its rating on the shares to Equal Weight from Overweight. The call questions how much more upside Wall Street can assign to a company whose artificial intelligence (AI) server business is still expanding quickly. That tension is now central to a broad pullback in enterprise hardware names tied to AI demand. Meanwhile, Hewlett Packard Enterprise (NYSE:HPE) stock is down 5% to $65.45 after drawing the same downgrade from Barclays. Additionally, Super Micro Computer (NASDAQ:SMCI) stock is down 4% to $37.37, a lighter decline than Dell’s. Hewlett Packard Enterprise sells similar server and networking equipment to the same enterprise buyers, while Super Micro Computer builds comparable systems as a smaller specialist. Selling pressure is far greater in hardware than across the broader sector, as the iShares U.S. Technology ETF (NYSEARCA:IYW) is down 1%. Large-cap growth benchmarks are holding up even better, and the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) is down 0.9%, a much softer decline than the server makers are posting. Barclays Questions How Much AI Growth Is Priced In Barclays analyst Tim Long wrote that valuations across corporate-focused hardware names have run too far and that he doesn’t yet see a meaningful AI inflection in enterprise spending. Long lowered his price target on Dell stock to $574 and on Hewlett Packard Enterprise shares to $77. He still expects Dell and Hewlett Packard Enterprise to top earnings estimates, though he argued the scale of those surprises is likely to become much smaller. Long’s downgrade takes aim at valuation. That leaves Dell’s AI server growth outlook intact, so the real debate centers on how much good news Dell stock already reflects after its strong run. Separately, Accenture and Dell announced an expanded partnership on October 9. The deal is built around a dedicated private AI business group, aimed at customers who want to run those workloads inside their own data centers. Dell sells servers, storage and personal computers, and its recent growth has come from configuring and shipping AI computing racks built around other companies’ chips. That’s a high-volume business earning thin margins on expensive hardware. When upside surprises shrink, a business built on shipping volume has less room to impress on profitability, which can leave Dell stock more exposed to valuation concerns. Enterprise buyers sit at the core of Dell’s AI exposure, which places the company directly in the path of Long’s concern about corporate spending, and Hewlett Packard Enterprise faces a similar question because it sells into many of the same corporate data centers. Such overlap helps explain why one analyst note is weighing on shares of Dell and Hewlett Packard Enterprise together. The next share-price move for Dell stock could depend on whether corporate customers start ordering AI hardware at the scale its valuation already assumes. Long’s call frames that as an unresolved question. The Accenture partnership offers an early read on how quickly private AI demand takes shape (we featured seven suppliers riding the same data-center expansion, from power to cooling, in a free report). A parallel question hangs over Hewlett Packard Enterprise, which sells similar equipment to the same corporate buyers. Smaller beats from Dell would support the Barclays view, while another large upside surprise would challenge it, and any visible pickup in corporate AI orders could also ease the valuation pressure Long describes. pages.text:

HPE and Miami HEAT transform Kaseya Center fan experience with AI-native wireless connectivity powered by an HPE Self-Driving Network
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 10:09 AM CDT 4 min read
New Wi-Fi 7 and next-generation autonomous networking will deliver enhanced connected experiences for fans, staff and venue operations
Miami HEAT is using HPE's AI-native networking capabilities to improve connectivity across the venue, providing enhanced digital experiences for fans and staff.
The partnership introduces HPE's self-driving network capabilities to automatically optimize performance, reduce operational burden, and simplify troubleshooting.
The modernized infrastructure provides a scalable foundation for Kaseya Center to easily adapt to future technologies.
MIAMI, October 19, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--HPE (NYSE: HPE) and the Miami HEAT today announced a network modernization project at Kaseya Center designed to enhance connectivity and create a more intelligent, resilient digital foundation for fans, staff and venue operations. This connectivity refresh is part of a series of updates being made to the venue ahead of the 2026-2027 NBA season to improve the arena experience for attendees.
As one of the NBA's premier venues, Kaseya Center hosts events attended by tens of thousands of people with changing conditions and a slew of devices that put significant demands on its network infrastructure. To deliver a consistently high-performing connected experience across the arena, the Miami HEAT selected HPE to modernize both its wireless and wired infrastructure and establish Wi-Fi 7 connectivity.
The deployment combines HPE Aruba wireless outdoor and indoor access points and campus gateways with HPE Juniper switching that provides the power, bandwidth and capacity required to support high-density connectivity throughout the venue. HPE will also provide Arena Event Network Monitoring Assistance across five live events to help validate and optimize network performance under real-world conditions.
"Today's sports and entertainment venues need networks that can deliver exceptional experiences for tens of thousands of people while also simplifying operations behind the scenes," said Rami Rahim, executive vice president, president and general manager, Networking at HPE. "Together with the Miami HEAT, we're building a self-driving network at Kaseya Center that is designed to improve connectivity, increase operational efficiency and create new possibilities for digital experiences for fans and staff."
Building the foundation for a more connected Kaseya Center
The project began with the Miami HEAT seeking to improve wireless performance in high-density areas of Kaseya Center, particularly the lower bowl. Through technical assessment and design, the effort expanded beyond a wireless refresh to include modernization of the underlying wired infrastructure required to support next-generation access points.
The new HPE networking infrastructure will help the Miami HEAT:
Deliver a Wi-Fi 7 experience for fans and staff across Kaseya Center
Improve wireless reliability and performance in high-density and critical seating areas
Provide the power and bandwidth required for next-generation wireless access points
Establish a modern network foundation that can support future digital experiences and venue innovation
Optimize performance during live events with self-driving operations, specialized network monitoring and tuning services
"Providing a reliable, seamless digital experience for everyone who enters Kaseya Center is critical, and important to us to ensure the best possible fan experience whether attending a HEAT game, a concert or another live event," said Drew Dorben, Vice President and CTO of the Miami HEAT. "With HPE, we're modernizing our digital foundation to better serve fans and staff today and into the future."
Advancing toward AI-driven, self-driving network operations
HPE's AI-native networking capabilities are designed to help organizations move from reactive network management toward increasingly autonomous operations. HPE's self-driving network uses AI-driven insights and automation to proactively identify and resolve connectivity issues, optimize performance and simplify troubleshooting, which helps IT teams maintain reliable connectivity while reducing the operational burden of managing increasingly complex environments.
For a high-density venue such as Kaseya Center, this approach provides the Miami HEAT with a scalable foundation to support evolving connectivity demands across basketball games, concerts and other major events.
The wireless deployment is expected to be completed ahead of the start of the 2026-2027 NBA season, with the broader campus switching modernization continuing in phases across the venue.
HPE is working with AT&T, which will provide communication services and CSPi Technology Solutions that will provide implementation expertise and ongoing managed IT services to support the networking environment.

Wall Street analysts reshuffled their bets Wednesday, hitting several major tech and industrial names with surprise downgrades while selectively upgrading defense and commodity plays. Find out which stocks just got a fresh vote of confidence and which ones lost favor.
Published October 14, 2026, 7:46am ET · 4 min read
Pre-Market Stock Futures:
Futures are trading mostly higher after a rather ho-hum start to the third-quarter earnings season. Large-cap financial stocks led off with strong numbers, though the sector’s results were mixed. JPMorgan Chase & Company (NYSE: JPM | JPM Price Prediction) reported strong results, but the firm’s fixed-income trading was down for the first time in two years, while Citigroup (NYSE: C) posted its best third-quarter revenue in a decade, as profits jumped 40% year-over-year, driven by a 6% rise in trading revenue. By Tuesday’s close, all major indices were modestly lower, with the small-cap Russell 2000 down the most, closing at 2,783, down 0.40%, while the Dow Jones Industrials fell 0.35% to 51,670. The tech-heavy Nasdaq closed down only 0.15% at 27,204 despite heavy selling in the chip sector, and the S&P 500 closed Tuesday’s session almost unchanged at 7,805, down only 0.02%.
Treasury Bonds:
After a day off for the Columbus Day holiday, bond markets returned to action Tuesday, with mixed trading as yields rose in shorter maturities and T-bills. In comparison, buyers eyed the belly of the curve and longer maturities, where yields were lower. By the close, the 30-year bond yield stood at 5.66%, while the 10-year note was last seen at 5.22%.
Oil and Gas:
Prices were mixed across the energy complex as heightened tensions across the Middle East continue to grow, with Saudi Arabia furious over the Houthi weekend attack on the Riyadh airport that killed 14 and wounded over 300, vowing a strong military resposne. Brent Crude closed Tuesday’s session at $106.10, down 0.48%, while West Texas Intermediate was last seen at $94.14, up 0.40%. Natural gas roared back from a slow start to the week, closing Tuesday at $3.28, up 3.66%.
Gold:
Gold was modestly lower on Tuesday; a stronger dollar, higher yields, and concerns over upcoming inflation data weighed on the bullion after a strong Monday. At the close, Gold was at $4,160, while Silver was last seen at $9.05, down 1.84%.
Crypto:
Crypto markets pulled a classic, volatile V-shaped recovery on Tuesday, clawing back steep losses from an overnight global stock slump driven by a sell-off in Asian tech and chip shares. Because crypto never sleeps and trades 24/7, Bitcoin dipped sharply to an early low near $81,000 before staging a rapid comeback, surging back over $84,000 Tuesday afternoon and ultimately stabilizing around $83,300 to $83,500 later in the day. At 8 AM EDT, Bitcoin was trading at $83,295, while Ethereum was quoted at $2,498.

Ryder Cup tech spotlight and AI data center win put Hewlett Packard Enterprise in focus
Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) has drawn fresh attention after a US$1.2 billion AMD Helios AI Rack order from Vultr and plans to run self-driving networking at the 2027 Ryder Cup in Ireland.
Recent trading suggests investors are treating Hewlett Packard Enterprise as an AI infrastructure and networking story rather than a slow-moving hardware vendor. The 1-month share price return of 38.63% and year-to-date share price gain of 198.26% point to strong momentum, while a 1-year total shareholder return of 181.39% and 5-year total shareholder return of 460.84% show that confidence has been building over multiple years as new deals and headline events, such as the Vultr contract and Ryder Cup partnership, have landed.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) Stock Gets Fair Value Bump As Analysts Split On AI Momentum
The fair value estimate for Hewlett Packard Enterprise has shifted from US$65.56 to US$68.08, a modest change that still matters if you are tracking valuation closely. This tweak reflects a divided analyst view, with supportive commentary pointing to strong server, cloud and AI orders, and more cautious voices focusing on networking supply constraints and the sharp share price move earlier in 2026. As you read on, you will see how to follow this evolving Hewlett Packard Enterprise narrative and what to watch next in the research.
Analyst Price Targets don't always capture the full story. Head over to our Company Report to find new ways to value Hewlett Packard Enterprise.
Several firms, including Citi, Barclays, BofA, Raymond James, Truist, Morgan Stanley and Deutsche Bank, have raised price targets on Hewlett Packard Enterprise, citing strong Q3 results, Cloud and AI order strength, and higher guidance for FY26 and FY27.
Networking is a key focus in recent research. Morgan Stanley and Barclays highlight networking as an important earnings driver, supported by AI demand, new products and expected Juniper synergies.
Wells Fargo and Citi comment on record or robust backlog and multi year supply commitments, which they indicate support visibility on future revenue and free cash flow for Hewlett Packard Enterprise.
Deutsche Bank notes that roughly two thirds of HPE's reported US$6.3b AI backlog is in enterprise and sovereign customers, which it characterizes as attractive for higher margin networking attach and software or integration opportunities.
Evercore ISI recently downgraded Hewlett Packard Enterprise to In Line, citing valuation following a very large year to date share price gain and fewer near term catalysts for further multiple expansion.
Evercore ISI and Piper Sandler flag networking supply constraints and concerns about the company meeting demand, with Piper Sandler also questioning how exposed HPE is to the areas of end market strength and raising the risk of peaking revenue and margins.

The net profit margin assumption is now about 9.81%, compared with roughly 8.55% previously.

The discount rate has changed from 9.43% to about 9.23%.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise (NYSE:HPE) has spent the past month convincing the market that its networking business drives its role in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure. Shares of Hewlett Packard Enterprise are trading at $72.70, up 40% over the past month, after two company announcements reset expectations for that business.
HPE Price Target — 24/7 Wall St.
Meanwhile, Super Micro Computer (NASDAQ:SMCI) stock is at $44.79, up 13% over the same period, a solid gain that still trails Hewlett Packard Enterprise stock by a wide margin. For its part, Dell Technologies (NYSE:DELL) stock is at $580.40, up 11% over the past month, a pace similar to that of Super Micro Computer stock.
For sector-wide gauges, the iShares U.S. Technology ETF (NYSEARCA:IYW) is at $271.51 and the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) trades at $757.24; these funds are up 7% and 5%, respectively, over the past month. That spread, with Hewlett Packard Enterprise stock far ahead of both rivals and both funds, marks a company-specific re-rating inside a sector that rose at a much slower clip.
Why Didn't HPE Make The Top 10 List?
24/7 Wall St has helped investors make money for over two decades, and our top analysts just finished ranking the definitive Top 10 Stocks To Buy Now. Not the ten biggest companies. Not the ten everyone is arguing about. The ten best stocks to buy right now.
And HPE didn't make the cut!
The report is free, and you can see why we think each stock is a top investment today.
A Helios Order and a Higher Networking Outlook
On September 30, Hewlett Packard Enterprise secured its first order for Helios AI rack systems, a $1.2 billion agreement with cloud provider Vultr covering deployments across Vultr's data centers in the United States. Under that deal, Hewlett Packard Enterprise is providing the networking layer, including Ethernet switches built on its Juniper technology, along with liquid cooling and deployment services.
At an investor day the same day, Hewlett Packard Enterprise raised its networking revenue growth outlook for the coming fiscal year into a high-teens to low-twenties percentage range. The company also set long-term targets. It projected its data center networking revenue to compound at a low-to-high fifties percentage rate over the following years, and it targeted its networking operating margins in the mid-to-high twenties as a percentage.
Why Networking Sets Hewlett Packard Enterprise Apart
Hewlett Packard Enterprise sells servers, storage and networking to data center operators, and the Juniper acquisition made networking the part of its business carrying the growth story. Because of that shift, a networking outlook carries outsized weight for Hewlett Packard Enterprise stock. Even the Vultr relationship traces back to Juniper, since Hewlett Packard Enterprise inherited it through that acquisition.
Super Micro Computer assembles servers built around other companies' processors, with little services revenue beside them. Dell sells servers and storage into the same buyers, with a large services business attached. All three capture data center spending, yet only Hewlett Packard Enterprise is being valued on a networking franchise.
Both September 30 announcements from Hewlett Packard Enterprise fell inside the past-month window, and they separate the company from Super Micro Computer and Dell. Shares of each of those rivals climbed over the same month while trailing Hewlett Packard Enterprise stock by a wide margin, and the two technology funds advanced by less still.
HPE Analyst Ratings — 24/7 Wall St.
The Vultr order supports the case for Hewlett Packard Enterprise, showing the company can win the networking layer of an AI buildout on top of the servers. Hewlett Packard Enterprise's raised savings target adds support, since the company now expects $800 million in annual run-rate cost savings from the Juniper acquisition, a figure that makes the deal look stronger than before.
A 40% gain in Hewlett Packard Enterprise stock in a single month, however, prices a great deal of that progress into the share price. Several pieces of the company's outlook cover years that haven't happened yet, and one order from one customer still amounts to a single data point.
Super Micro Computer stock and Dell stock rising far less over the same month is what makes the move in Hewlett Packard Enterprise stock company-specific, a distinction that cuts both ways since a re-rating built on one company's announcements could reverse if Hewlett Packard Enterprise's next update falls short.
Investors can watch for a second Helios platform customer, which would show whether the Vultr order at Hewlett Packard Enterprise begins a pattern, as a follow-on win would strengthen the case for the company's networking push while a long gap could leave Hewlett Packard Enterprise stock leaning on one deal.
Shareholders may want to keep an eye on whether Hewlett Packard Enterprise's networking growth rate holds within the high-teens to low-twenties percentage range the company outlined for the coming fiscal year. Reaching that range would support Hewlett Packard Enterprise stock at its new level, while a slowdown could hand back part of the past month's gain.
Hewlett Packard Enterprise now pairs a stronger networking story with a far higher share price than a month ago. Share positions should reflect both the promise of the Vultr order and the speed of a 40% one-month run in HPE stock.

HPE Spaceborne Computer to Power High Performance Computing and AI on the Moon
HPE Spaceborne Computer-4, an advanced compute module built for space environments, plans to power artificial intelligence (AI) and the first high performance computing (HPC) benchmarks on the surface of the Moon.
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 9:00 AM CDT 5 min read
NASA, Deloitte, and HPE to deploy AI workloads on HPE's Spaceborne Computer-4 to maximize the mission's scientific discovery
With 70 years of leadership in space exploration, HPE ushers in a new era by providing the advanced computing foundation for the emerging lunar economy
HPE Spaceborne Computer-4 plans to power the first high performance computing benchmarks on the lunar surface
HPE Spaceborne Computer-4 will test large language model (LLM) retrieval-augmented generation, vision inference, and LiDAR data for reliable deployment of AI on the Moon
HOUSTON, October 20, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--HPE today announced HPE Spaceborne Computer-4, an advanced compute module built for space environments, plans to power artificial intelligence (AI) and the first high performance computing (HPC) benchmarks on the surface of the Moon1. The system will deploy on Astrolab's FLIP rover for an upcoming mission for the Moon Base program and will test the suitability of advanced computing for future missions and the emerging lunar economy.
"For more than 70 years, HPE innovation has supported some of the world's most important space missions. The next chapter of lunar exploration will depend on the ability to turn data into insights at the point of discovery," said Scott Wiest, vice president, fellow and global sales chief technologist, HPE. "With HPE Spaceborne Computer-4, we are bringing AI and high performance computing to the lunar edge, helping the acceleration of scientific discovery and building the infrastructure for the next era of exploration."
The mission is intended to launch in late 2026 as part of NASA's Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) initiative. After touching down near the lunar South Pole region, Voyager Technologies' Griffin-1 lander will transport Astrolab's FLIP rover, carrying HPE Spaceborne Computer-4 as a payload.
"The Moon presents a challenging environment for advanced computing, and we're pleased to provide HPE with an opportunity to demonstrate its technology on the lunar surface," said Jaret Matthews, founder and CEO of Astrolab. "Our FLIP rover is designed to accommodate a variety of payloads, and this mission will demonstrate how commercial lunar mobility platforms can support technology development and scientific research."
AI workloads and first-ever HPC to run on the Moon's surface
During the mission, HPE Spaceborne Computer-4 is scheduled to run core AI applications and the first high performance computing2 benchmarks on the Moon. The test results from these experiments will help create the technological foundation required for future missions and research on the Moon's surface. Large language models (LLM) will deliver insights, analyze visual data, and support autonomous monitoring at the lunar edge. Additional tests will process LiDAR data for mapping, navigation, terrain analysis and infrastructure development, while an AI services container will demonstrate reliable deployment of scalable AI service applications on the Moon.
HPE Spaceborne Computer-4 is purpose-built as a lightweight, self-contained, and fanless compute module designed to survive the harsh environment of the lunar South pole. It is equipped with both a low-power central process unit (CPU) and graphics processing unit (GPU). The compute module utilizes flash memory storage inside solid state drives from KIOXIA, continuing a long-standing collaboration with the HPE Spaceborne program to support the missions' activities and tests with high performance data storage under lunar conditions. HPE also assembled an extensive software suite that optimizes the required interaction with Earth-based resources and enables secure delivery of insights and results from the Moon back to Earth.
In addition, HPE will support Astrolab's mission control in Hawthorne, California using HPE Private Cloud to support real-time insights, delivered in a turnkey solution. In addition, HPE CloudOps Software will provide a unified, flexible environment for managing and automating workloads.
Private-public partnerships help maximize the mission's scientific return
NASA and Deloitte are set to join HPE Spaceborne Computer-4 to deploy AI workloads on the Moon and perform advanced solutions critical for maximizing the scientific return, underpinning the success of the emerging lunar economy.

HPE just posted its worst week ever after a single analyst downgrade, yet its earnings are surging and its backlog hit a record high. The real question is whether the market sees a danger that the numbers are hiding.
Published October 20, 2026, 7:31am ET · 4 min read
Two professionals analyze market data and financial trends on a laptop, mirroring the optimistic outlook and raised price targets for companies like HPE. © VideoFlow / Shutterstock.com
Shares of Hewlett Packard Enterprise (NYSE:HPE | HPE Price Prediction) fell 20.56% in the week through October 19. It was its worst week ever, following an October 14 analyst downgrade that questioned HPE’s AI growth.
The drop hit a stock that already traded at a forward PE of roughly 12 to 15, while the broader market averages 30. Investors Dave Ahern and Stephen Morris recently debated whether that gap makes HPE an opportunity or a value trap.
Ahern asked: “Is that a lifetime opportunity, or does Wall Street know something that the rest of value investors maybe don’t know? Like, why is it so cheap?” The question is pressing because the results are strong.
Revenue in the fiscal third quarter rose 32.7% to $12.21 billion. Non-GAAP EPS of $1.11 beat the $0.93 consensus.
Morris rated HPE’s moat today as “next to non-existent,” and that view accounts for most of the discount.
A 12x Multiple Signals Doubt About Durability
A forward PE divides the share price by expected earnings. A low multiple therefore means investors doubt those estimates will hold, and the market is currently pricing in a fade in AI server demand.
The trailing P/E of 1300x is distorted by Juniper integration charges and a fiscal 2025 goodwill impairment. That is why the hosts focus on the forward number.
Analysts’ average fiscal 2027 EPS estimate is $4.7088, up from $4.0384 90 days ago. None of those analysts revised down in the past 30 days.
Management’s own fiscal 2027 framework calls for EPS of $4.40 to $4.60. That range leaves out the Helios AI rack opportunity.
Wall Street Turned Cautious After a Huge Run
Even after falling 8.05% over the past month, HPE is still up 135.22% year to date and 147.52% over the past year. Shares rose 1.29% on October 19 to $55.84. The post-downgrade rebound was small.
Although the market has embraced HPE this year, it remains unclear whether AI-driven earnings will last long enough to justify that price. Still, orders grew faster than revenue, and backlog hit a record while memory shortages held back shipments.
Ahern’s long-term test sets the hype aside: “Forget the AI trade. What is a stock going to do 10 years from now?” AI server revenue fails that test because it is cyclical: orders shrink once data center buildouts slow, and nothing ties buyers to HPE.
Server revenue rose 35.3% to $6.77 billion on AI demand. Servers are a competitive, low-margin business, and customers switch suppliers over price, which is why the picks-and-shovels names behind the AI expansion (power, cooling, networking) often look more durable than the box makers; we rounded up seven of them in a free report here.
Management expects gross margin to return to historical levels as AI systems take up a larger share of sales. It guides Cloud and AI operating margin to about 13% in fiscal 2027.
Juniper Is HPE’s First Real Shot at a Moat
HPE closed its Juniper Networks acquisition and sold its remaining 19% stake in China-based H3C in May 2026. Together, those moves changed its business mix toward networking.
Networking gear is built into how a customer runs its operations, and it costs a lot to replace. The segment earned a 22% operating margin last quarter. With Juniper included, networking revenue jumped 74.9% to $2.89 billion, and orders rose 36%.
GreenLake lets customers pay for infrastructure as a service inside their own data centers, and it reached 52,000 customers, up 18%. Rising net retention would point to recurring revenue, while flat usage would suggest customers use it to finance hardware.
Discussing the chief executive’s vision, Morris said “the uncertainty around that statement is very high,” but added that if it “comes to fruition,” HPE “will be significantly untouchable.” Juniper likely moves HPE’s moat from absent to plausible, although the integration still has to prove it can hold customers.
HPE’s case looks strongest under Ahern’s 10-year test. The weekly drop and a forward multiple far below the market’s already price in heavy doubt.
Juniper savings are on track for a $600 million annual run rate by fiscal 2028. Meanwhile, a 1.07% dividend yield on a $74.1 billion company provides some income.
The thesis breaks if networking growth stalls after the integration, if GreenLake fails to become recurring revenue, or if AI server demand falls faster than networking can make up for it. Fiscal fourth-quarter results come next. Revenue is guided to $13.9 billion to $14.8 billion, and management has promised a fuller fiscal 2027 outlook.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) Stock: Rises as Miami HEAT Taps HPE for Wi-Fi 7 Upgrade
HPE Stock Gains as Miami HEAT Selects Wi-Fi 7 Technology to Modernize Kaseya Center Ahead of NBA Season
By Yasmin WernerOctober 19, 2026No Comments3 Mins Read
HPE stock climbs 1.29% to $55.84 following a new Miami HEAT networking deal.
Miami HEAT taps HPE to bring faster Wi-Fi 7 connectivity to Kaseya Center fans.
HPE Aruba access points and Juniper switches will modernize arena connectivity.
HPE will test and optimize arena network performance across five live events.
AT&T and CSPi will support the network rollout ahead of the 2026–27 NBA season.
Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) stock gained 1.29% to close at $55.84 on Monday, October 19. Shares added 0.05% to $55.87 after hours, despite afternoon selling pressure. HPE also announced a Miami HEAT project to upgrade Kaseya Center’s connectivity.
HPE Stock Advances as Arena Upgrades Expand
HPE will overhaul wireless access and supporting wired systems ahead of the 2026–27 NBA season. For the Miami HEAT, the project forms part of broader improvements to the venue’s digital infrastructure. These improvements target fan access, staff communication, and systems that support daily arena operations.
Kaseya Center hosts basketball games, concerts, and other events that attract large crowds. Heavy device use can strain wireless networks, especially where spectators sit close together. The HEAT initially focused on improving coverage in crowded seating sections, including the lower bowl.
However, a technical review showed that faster wireless access also required upgrades to existing wired equipment. As a result, the project expanded to address network switching and power delivery. The broader scope will help the venue handle modern access points and future digital services.
Wi-Fi 7 Upgrade Targets High-Density Connectivity
Under the plan, HPE will install Aruba indoor and outdoor wireless access points across the site. Campus gateways will manage traffic, while HPE Juniper switches will supply the required bandwidth and capacity. Together, the equipment will establish Wi-Fi 7 connectivity for fans and staff.
Wi-Fi 7 supports greater network capacity in busy locations with large numbers of connected devices. At Kaseya Center, the upgrade targets reliable performance during games and other major events. It also aims to limit connection problems in critical seating areas and operational spaces.
HPE will provide specialized network monitoring support during five live events. Those sessions will test network behavior under real crowds and changing traffic conditions. Engineers can then tune performance using event data rather than relying only on initial tests.
HPE plans to use AI-assisted network tools to identify faults and improve performance. Its automation can simplify troubleshooting and reduce manual work for arena technology teams. This approach will support network operations as demand changes across different event schedules.
AT&T will provide communication services for the updated network environment. CSPi Technology Solutions will supply implementation support and ongoing managed IT services. These roles will connect the hardware deployment with its practical operation after installation.
HPE expects to finish the wireless rollout before the new NBA season starts. The company will continue switching upgrades across the arena in phases. For HPE, the agreement extends its networking work into another high-traffic entertainment setting.

Learn Why The Bull Case For HPE Stock Could Change Following Gen13 Server Launch
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 7:22 PM CDT 6 min read
Hewlett Packard Enterprise announced its first HPE ProLiant Gen13 Servers powered by 6th Gen AMD EPYC processors, adding higher core density, expanded memory and I/O, and new security features such as automatic self encrypting drives, multi person authorization, and extended post quantum cryptography readiness.
The ProLiant Gen13 lineup targets AI inference, agentic AI workflows, data intensive simulations, and financial modeling, which speaks directly to HPE's push into higher value compute, security centric infrastructure, and rack level efficiency for customers modernizing data centers and hybrid cloud environments.
We will now look at how Hewlett Packard Enterprise's investment narrative could be influenced by these ProLiant Gen13 AI focused servers.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise Investment Narrative Recap
An investor in Hewlett Packard Enterprise needs to believe the business can turn strong AI and networking demand into delivered systems, higher margin services, and durable recurring revenue. The latest ProLiant Gen13 and Cray XD launches point to that direction, but the near term swing factor still looks like execution on AI infrastructure orders and Juniper integration rather than any single product win.
The biggest near term risk remains a mismatch between robust orders and what actually ships into data center and hybrid cloud projects, especially now that guidance already incorporates healthy AI server and networking expectations. Valuation stretch and insider selling add sensitivity to any slip in AI deal timing, networking CAGRs, or margin delivery.
The Mizuho Securities deployment of HPE Cray XD2000 with direct liquid cooling is the clearest operational tie in to the new ProLiant Gen13 story. Both point to Hewlett Packard Enterprise leaning into high density, liquid cooled compute for workloads that resemble AI training and inference, complex financial modeling, and large scale simulations.
For catalysts, this type of reference project matters because it tests HPE's ability to scale advanced cooling, maintain performance per kilowatt, and wrap it with monitoring and services. Any delays in bringing the new Mizuho data center into production or in expanding beyond the initial eight nodes would feed directly into the existing risk around converting AI infrastructure demand into recognized revenue.
Hewlett Packard Enterprise Forecasts Behind the AI Server Push
Hewlett Packard Enterprise's AI centric server roadmap plugs into a much bigger earnings story that analysts have already mapped out. The projections assume the business can convert ProLiant Gen13, Cray XD, and Juniper powered networking into steadier profit instead of just one off hardware spikes.
Consensus forecasts point to Hewlett Packard Enterprise's revenue rising by 14.3% a year over the next three years, with earnings expected to climb from US$2.7b today to US$6.1b by 2029. That implies earnings a little more than doubling from the current base if the forecast plays out as modeled.
On top of that profit bridge, analysts are baking in margin expansion from 6.4% today to 9.8% in three years, helped by a higher mix from AI infrastructure, data center networking, and recurring GreenLake style services tied to deployments like the new ProLiant Gen13 servers. The story is not just about selling more hardware. It is about attaching software, monitoring, and financing so that more of each data center dollar shows up as net income.
Those expectations are not perfectly aligned. Some research teams see earnings reaching as high as US$7.3b by 2029, which would require an even stronger uplift from AI centric networking and data center projects than the base case. For readers, that spread in outcomes is a reminder to stress test personal models for slower AI uptake, longer Juniper integration timelines, or more muted margin progress alongside the upside scenarios.
Valuation assumptions sit on top of these operating forecasts. To support current analyst targets, Hewlett Packard Enterprise would need to trade on a P/E of 19.9x applied to the 2029 earnings estimate, compared with 34.1x today. That would represent a lower multiple than the 27.4x currently cited for the broader US tech industry, which places more of the burden on actual execution in AI infrastructure rather than on multiple expansion.
Hewlett Packard Enterprise's narrative projects US$62.5b revenue and US$6.1b earnings by 2029. This requires 14.3% yearly revenue growth and an earnings increase from US$2.7b.

AI Financing Doubts Extend the Hardware Selloff
Pressure on Hewlett Packard Enterprise stock extends a selloff in AI hardware as investors question how AI infrastructure spending gets financed. Data center buildouts demand heavy upfront expenditures. Doubts about who funds them flow straight back to the companies that sell the equipment, including Hewlett Packard Enterprise. Barclays heightened that debate on Wednesday when it cut its ratings on Hewlett Packard Enterprise and Dell to the equivalent of hold. The firm argued that businesses haven’t yet meaningfully increased their AI spending and that recent hardware revenue strength owes more to higher memory component prices.
Broader technology funds are slipping by smaller margins. The iShares U.S. Technology ETF (NYSEARCA:IYW) is down 2%. Large-cap tech is holding up even better (though it’s still selling off), as the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) is down 1.3%.
Networking Growth Versus Component Price Risk
The upside story for Hewlett Packard Enterprise rests on AI server demand and its expanded networking business. Networking gives the company a second growth engine alongside servers, which could buffer Hewlett Packard Enterprise if AI server orders cool.
Hewlett Packard Enterprise is still integrating Juniper Networks into its networking business, so much of the payoff depends on execution. Integration work can absorb management focus at a time when hardware demand faces fresh questions.
On the bear side, slower enterprise AI spending could leave the hardware growth at Hewlett Packard Enterprise tied to component prices. Under that view, revenue could cool once memory pricing settles down, even if customer orders hold steady.
Corporate AI budgets sit at the center of this debate. Will businesses begin to lift that spending? The next test for Hewlett Packard Enterprise is whether they do so in a way that backs up its server and networking story. Clear signs of broader enterprise adoption could ease the financing worries weighing on Hewlett Packard Enterprise stock.
Memory pricing is the other open variable for Hewlett Packard Enterprise, since Barclays tied much of the recent hardware revenue strength to higher component prices. Investors can watch for whether the gap between Hewlett Packard Enterprise stock and the broader technology funds (IYW and QQQ) narrows as the financing debate plays out.
Hewlett Packard Enterprise still holds a credible growth path through AI servers and its expanded networking business, but the hardware group is trading on financing doubts for now. Traders may prefer to keep their HPE share exposure small until the enterprise AI spending question resolves.
