Barclays Questions How Much AI Growth Is Priced In
Barclays analyst Tim Long wrote that valuations across corporate-focused hardware names have run too far and that he doesn’t yet see a meaningful AI inflection in enterprise spending. Long lowered his price target on Dell stock to $574 and on Hewlett Packard Enterprise shares to $77. He still expects Dell and Hewlett Packard Enterprise to top earnings estimates, though he argued the scale of those surprises is likely to become much smaller.
Long’s downgrade takes aim at valuation. That leaves Dell’s AI server growth outlook intact, so the real debate centers on how much good news Dell stock already reflects after its strong run. Separately, Accenture and Dell announced an expanded partnership on October 9. The deal is built around a dedicated private AI business group, aimed at customers who want to run those workloads inside their own data centers.
Dell sells servers, storage and personal computers, and its recent growth has come from configuring and shipping AI computing racks built around other companies’ chips. That’s a high-volume business earning thin margins on expensive hardware. When upside surprises shrink, a business built on shipping volume has less room to impress on profitability, which can leave Dell stock more exposed to valuation concerns.
Enterprise buyers sit at the core of Dell’s AI exposure, which places the company directly in the path of Long’s concern about corporate spending, and Hewlett Packard Enterprise faces a similar question because it sells into many of the same corporate data centers. Such overlap helps explain why one analyst note is weighing on shares of Dell and Hewlett Packard Enterprise together.
The next share-price move for Dell stock could depend on whether corporate customers start ordering AI hardware at the scale its valuation already assumes. Long’s call frames that as an unresolved question. The Accenture partnership offers an early read on how quickly private AI demand takes shape (we featured seven suppliers riding the same data-center expansion, from power to cooling, in a free report). A parallel question hangs over Hewlett Packard Enterprise, which sells similar equipment to the same corporate buyers.
Smaller beats from Dell would support the Barclays view, while another large upside surprise would challenge it, and any visible pickup in corporate AI orders could also ease the valuation pressure Long describes. Investors should consider keeping their position sizes modest until enterprise ordering patterns become clearer.

HPE and Miami HEAT transform Kaseya Center fan experience with AI-native wireless connectivity powered by an HPE Self-Driving Network
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 10:09 AM CDT 4 min read
New Wi-Fi 7 and next-generation autonomous networking will deliver enhanced connected experiences for fans, staff and venue operations
Miami HEAT is using HPE's AI-native networking capabilities to improve connectivity across the venue, providing enhanced digital experiences for fans and staff.
The partnership introduces HPE's self-driving network capabilities to automatically optimize performance, reduce operational burden, and simplify troubleshooting.
The modernized infrastructure provides a scalable foundation for Kaseya Center to easily adapt to future technologies.
MIAMI, October 19, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--HPE (NYSE: HPE) and the Miami HEAT today announced a network modernization project at Kaseya Center designed to enhance connectivity and create a more intelligent, resilient digital foundation for fans, staff and venue operations. This connectivity refresh is part of a series of updates being made to the venue ahead of the 2026-2027 NBA season to improve the arena experience for attendees.
As one of the NBA's premier venues, Kaseya Center hosts events attended by tens of thousands of people with changing conditions and a slew of devices that put significant demands on its network infrastructure. To deliver a consistently high-performing connected experience across the arena, the Miami HEAT selected HPE to modernize both its wireless and wired infrastructure and establish Wi-Fi 7 connectivity.
The deployment combines HPE Aruba wireless outdoor and indoor access points and campus gateways with HPE Juniper switching that provides the power, bandwidth and capacity required to support high-density connectivity throughout the venue. HPE will also provide Arena Event Network Monitoring Assistance across five live events to help validate and optimize network performance under real-world conditions.
"Today's sports and entertainment venues need networks that can deliver exceptional experiences for tens of thousands of people while also simplifying operations behind the scenes," said Rami Rahim, executive vice president, president and general manager, Networking at HPE. "Together with the Miami HEAT, we're building a self-driving network at Kaseya Center that is designed to improve connectivity, increase operational efficiency and create new possibilities for digital experiences for fans and staff."
Building the foundation for a more connected Kaseya Center
The project began with the Miami HEAT seeking to improve wireless performance in high-density areas of Kaseya Center, particularly the lower bowl. Through technical assessment and design, the effort expanded beyond a wireless refresh to include modernization of the underlying wired infrastructure required to support next-generation access points.
The new HPE networking infrastructure will help the Miami HEAT:
Deliver a Wi-Fi 7 experience for fans and staff across Kaseya Center
Improve wireless reliability and performance in high-density and critical seating areas
Provide the power and bandwidth required for next-generation wireless access points
Establish a modern network foundation that can support future digital experiences and venue innovation
Optimize performance during live events with self-driving operations, specialized network monitoring and tuning services
"Providing a reliable, seamless digital experience for everyone who enters Kaseya Center is critical, and important to us to ensure the best possible fan experience whether attending a HEAT game, a concert or another live event," said Drew Dorben, Vice President and CTO of the Miami HEAT. "With HPE, we're modernizing our digital foundation to better serve fans and staff today and into the future."
Advancing toward AI-driven, self-driving network operations
HPE's AI-native networking capabilities are designed to help organizations move from reactive network management toward increasingly autonomous operations. HPE's self-driving network uses AI-driven insights and automation to proactively identify and resolve connectivity issues, optimize performance and simplify troubleshooting, which helps IT teams maintain reliable connectivity while reducing the operational burden of managing increasingly complex environments.
For a high-density venue such as Kaseya Center, this approach provides the Miami HEAT with a scalable foundation to support evolving connectivity demands across basketball games, concerts and other major events.
The wireless deployment is expected to be completed ahead of the start of the 2026-2027 NBA season, with the broader campus switching modernization continuing in phases across the venue.
HPE is working with AT&T, which will provide communication services and CSPi Technology Solutions that will provide implementation expertise and ongoing managed IT services to support the networking environment.

HPE reports fiscal 2026 third quarter results
Record results and demand drive higher outlook for fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2027
-Record revenue of $12.2 billion, up 34% year-over-year
-Record operating profit, with GAAP OP up 464% and non-GAAP OP up 155% year-over-year
HOUSTON – September 2, 2026 – HPE (NYSE: HPE) today announced financial results for the third quarter ended July 31, 2026.
“HPE’s strategy is proving itself again this quarter. Our results demonstrate the durability of our profitable growth momentum. We delivered record revenue, orders, and profitability, fueled by surging customer demand across our portfolio,” said Antonio Neri, president and CEO of HPE. “AI is becoming a multi-year growth driver for HPE, and our differentiated portfolio positions us to capture that opportunity at scale.”
“Our outstanding revenue performance and expanded profitability in the third quarter reflect robust demand across our portfolio and consistent, disciplined execution,” said Marie Myers, executive vice president and CFO of HPE. “With our Q3 results and our order backlog at a record level, we are raising our financial outlook and plan to return at least 75% of free cash flow to shareholders in Q4.”
Third Quarter Fiscal 2026 Financial Results
•Revenue: $12.2 billion, up 34% from the prior-year period
•Gross margins:
◦GAAP of 40.1%, up 1,090 basis points from the prior-year period and up 360 basis points sequentially
◦Non-GAAP(1) of 40.4%, up 1,050 basis points from the prior-year period and up 350 basis points sequentially
•Operating profit margins:
◦GAAP of 11.4%, up 870 basis points from the prior-year period and up 440 basis points sequentially
◦Non-GAAP(1) of 16.2%, up 770 basis points from the prior-year period and up 290 basis points sequentially
•Diluted net earnings per share (“EPS”):
◦GAAP of $1.06, up $0.85 from the prior-year period and above our outlook range of $0.84 - $0.89
◦Non-GAAP(1) of $1.11, up $0.67 from the prior-year period and above our outlook range of $0.88 - $0.93
•Cash flow from operations: $1.6 billion, an increase of $0.3 billion from the prior-year period
•Free cash flow(1)(2): $1.0 billion, an increase of $0.2 billion from the prior-year period
•Capital returns to common shareholders: $324 million in the form of dividends and share repurchases
Third Quarter Fiscal 2026 Segment Results
•Networking revenue was $2.9 billion, up 74.9% from the prior-year period, with 22.0% operating profit margin, compared to 22.1% from the prior-year period.
◦Within Networking, revenue from:
▪Campus & Branch was $1.4 billion, up 31.0% from the prior-year period.
▪Data Center Networking was $382 million, up 112.2% from the prior-year period.
▪Security was $281 million, up 75.6% from the prior-year period.
▪Routing was $788 million, up 270.0% from the prior-year period.
•Cloud & AI revenue was $9.0 billion, up 25.4% from the prior-year period, with 17.0% operating profit margin, compared to 7.0% from the prior-year period.
◦Within Cloud & AI, revenue from:
▪Server was $6.8 billion, up 35.3% from the prior-year period.
▪Storage was $1.3 billion, up 10.2% from the prior-year period.
▪Financial Services was $0.9 billion, down 0.3% from the prior-year period.
•Corporate Investments and Other revenue was $278 million, up 3.0% from the prior-year period, with -24.1% of operating profit margin, compared to -7.0% from the prior-year period.
The HPE Board of Directors declared a regular cash dividend of $0.1425 per share on the company’s common stock, payable on or about October 16, 2026, to stockholders of record as of the close of business on September 17, 2026.
HPE estimates revenue to be in the range of $13.9 billion to $14.8 billion. HPE estimates GAAP diluted net EPS to be in the range of $1.12 to $1.22 and non-GAAP diluted net EPS(1) to be in the range of $1.20 to $1.30. Fiscal 2026 fourth quarter non-GAAP diluted net EPS estimate excludes net after-tax
adjustments of approximately $0.08 per diluted share, primarily related to amortization of intangible assets, stock-based compensation expense, acquisition, disposition and other charges, and cost reduction program.
HPE is raising its FY26 revenue growth outlook range to 34% to 37%. HPE is raising revenue growth expectations for the Networking segment to 73% to 74%. HPE estimates GAAP operating profit growth range to be 1,070% to 1,105% and non-GAAP operating profit growth range between 100% to 105%(1)(3).
HPE is raising both GAAP diluted net EPS to be in the range of $2.93 to $3.03 and non-GAAP diluted net EPS(1) to be in the range of $3.75 to $3.85. Fiscal 2026 non-GAAP diluted net EPS estimate excludes net after-tax adjustments of approximately $0.82 per diluted share, primarily related to amortization of intangible assets, stock-based compensation expense, acquisition, disposition and other charges, cost reduction program, and adjustments related to the sale of H3C. HPE is also raising its free cash flow(1)(2)(4) guidance and now expects free cash flow to be at least $3.75 billion.
The company is raising its growth framework for FY27. HPE is raising its revenue growth outlook range to 13% to 17%. HPE is raising expectations for non-GAAP diluted net EPS growth to be in the range of 16% to 20%(1)(4). HPE estimates non-GAAP operating margin rate to be in the range of 14% to 15%(1)(4). HPE is also raising its free cash flow guidance and now expects free cash flow to be at least $5.0 billion(1)(2)(4).
1 A description of HPE’s use of non-GAAP financial information is provided below under “Use of non-GAAP financial information and key performance metrics.”
2 Free cash flow represents cash flow from operations, less net capital expenditures (investments in property, plant & equipment (“PP&E”) and software assets less proceeds from the sale of PP&E), and adjusted for the effect of exchange rate fluctuations on cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash.
3 FY26 non-GAAP operating profit excludes costs of approximately $2.5 billion primarily related to amortization of intangible assets, stock-based compensation expense, acquisition, disposition and other charges, and cost reduction program.

text: HPE Has a 12x Forward PE and 400% Growth. So Why Won’t Wall Street Touch It? HPE just posted its worst week ever after a single analyst downgrade, yet its earnings are surging and its backlog hit a record high. The real question is whether the market sees a danger that the numbers are hiding. Published October 20, 2026, 7:31am ET · 4 min read Two professionals analyze market data and financial trends on a laptop, mirroring the optimistic outlook and raised price targets for companies like HPE. © VideoFlow / Shutterstock.com Shares of Hewlett Packard Enterprise (NYSE:HPE | HPE Price Prediction) fell 20.56% in the week through October 19. It was its worst week ever, following an October 14 analyst downgrade that questioned HPE’s AI growth. The drop hit a stock that already traded at a forward PE of roughly 12 to 15, while the broader market averages 30. Investors Dave Ahern and Stephen Morris recently debated whether that gap makes HPE an opportunity or a value trap. Ahern asked: “Is that a lifetime opportunity, or does Wall Street know something that the rest of value investors maybe don’t know? Like, why is it so cheap?” The question is pressing because the results are strong. Revenue in the fiscal third quarter rose 32.7% to $12.21 billion. Non-GAAP EPS of $1.11 beat the $0.93 consensus. Morris rated HPE’s moat today as “next to non-existent,” and that view accounts for most of the discount. A 12x Multiple Signals Doubt About Durability A forward PE divides the share price by expected earnings. A low multiple therefore means investors doubt those estimates will hold, and the market is currently pricing in a fade in AI server demand. The trailing P/E of 1300x is distorted by Juniper integration charges and a fiscal 2025 goodwill impairment. That is why the hosts focus on the forward number. Analysts’ average fiscal 2027 EPS estimate is $4.7088, up from $4.0384 90 days ago. None of those analysts revised down in the past 30 days. Management’s own fiscal 2027 framework calls for EPS of $4.40 to $4.60. That range leaves out the Helios AI rack opportunity. Wall Street Turned Cautious After a Huge Run Even after falling 8.05% over the past month, HPE is still up 135.22% year to date and 147.52% over the past year. Shares rose 1.29% on October 19 to $55.84. The post-downgrade rebound was small. Although the market has embraced HPE this year, it remains unclear whether AI-driven earnings will last long enough to justify that price. Still, orders grew faster than revenue, and backlog hit a record while memory shortages held back shipments. Ahern’s long-term test sets the hype aside: “Forget the AI trade. What is a stock going to do 10 years from now?” AI server revenue fails that test because it is cyclical: orders shrink once data center buildouts slow, and nothing ties buyers to HPE. The system will deploy on Astrolab's FLIP rover for an upcoming mission for the Moon Base program and will test the suitability of advanced computing for future missions and the emerging lunar economy. "For more than 70 years, HPE innovation has supported some of the world's most important space missions. The next chapter of lunar exploration will depend on the ability to turn data into insights at the point of discovery," said Scott Wiest, vice president, fellow and global sales chief technologist, HPE. "With HPE Spaceborne Computer-4, we are bringing AI and high performance computing to the lunar edge, helping the acceleration of scientific discovery and building the infrastructure for the next era of exploration." The mission is intended to launch in late 2026 as part of NASA's Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) initiative. After touching down near the lunar South Pole region, Voyager Technologies' Griffin-1 lander will transport Astrolab's FLIP rover, carrying HPE Spaceborne Computer-4 as a payload.
